summary: Console alert fingerprint rotation causes duplicate notifications and missing cohort links after rollforward
description: Customer reports a spike in duplicate alert notifications and several alert digests missing cohort/drilldown links. Issue started shortly after a background rollforward of the retention compaction job and a hotfix that rotated the alert fingerprinting key for de-duplication.
impact: Many on-call engineers at BrightRoute are receiving repeated Slack/email notifications for the same incidents. Additionally, alert digests for historical windows do not include functional drilldown links to the cohort pages, blocking investigation and increasing MTTR.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run a query that triggers an alert with grouping by customer_route_id and cohort tags for a long-running prefix-cache rewrite
2) Observe alert firing and deduplication behavior in the console during/after retention compaction window
3) Check alert digest email/Slack payloads for duplicate entries and inspect drilldown URLs in the UI
4) Reproduce after toggling the rollout flag that rotates the alert fingerprinting salt (internal flag: alert.fingerprint.rotate)

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Maya): alerts duplicated only for rules with grouping keys that include high-cardinality route identifiers. Non-grouped alerts unaffected.

SRE (Omar): retention compaction backfill ran at 02:00 UTC; an emergency hotfix rotated the alert fingerprint salt at 02:10 UTC to address a separate collision bug (PR #10288). Timing overlap correlates with symptom onset.

Hypothesis: fingerprint salt rotation changed hash outputs for already-queued alert evaluations; notification dedupe relies on stable fingerprint across contiguous evaluation windows. When salt changed mid-wave, the same incident produced two different fingerprints and was delivered twice.

Cohort links: digests reference historical run ids whose link tokens were signed before a recent token-format migration. Link resolver now rejects those tokens, causing missing drilldown links in digest emails.
Reproduction: toggling alert.fingerprint.rotate=false on staging prevented duplicates during a simulated compaction backfill. Re-enabling rotation reproduced duplicates.

Additional observation: message dedupe in notify-slack checks (fingerprint, run_id). Because compaction backfill replays evaluation windows with new run ids, dedupe logic failed when fingerprint changed as well.

Related dashboards show elevated notify latency (~150ms) during the window, but not high enough to explain replays. No sign of retry storms from notify queue; duplicates appear to be generated upstream by alert-service.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Collected customer screenshots and sample alert IDs; shared initial logs and Slack channel details. Customer requests immediate mitigation to stop duplicate notifications.

Omar Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Disabled alert.fingerprint.rotate rollout flag in prod as temporary mitigation at 02:45 UTC. Notified BrightRoute of partial mitigation; duplicates stopped for new evaluations but historical digest links still broken.

Elena Ruiz (Product) - 2026-03-11: Escalated to Eng PMs for a coordinated fix: ensure fingerprint rotation never occurs during playback/backfill windows and issue a short-term soft-landing that maps previous fingerprint variants to canonical ids for 24h.
BrightRoute (Customer) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed reduction in duplicate Slack alerts. Still needs historical digests fixed for postmortem work. Provided a list of three missing digest run_ids.
Omar Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Rolled out a mapping shim in alert-service to treat the two most-recent fingerprint salts as equivalent for dedupe logic for 48h. Monitoring for false suppression.
resolution: Mitigations applied: 1) Disabled immediate fingerprint rotation rollout flag to stop new duplicates. 2) Deployed a 48h fingerprint compatibility shim to coalesce recent salts for dedupe. 3) Created a separate short-lived token-resolver job to regenerate valid drilldown tokens for the three missing digest run_ids provided by the customer. Long-term fix: engineering to implement rotation-safe dedupe that ties dedupe window to stable evaluation run ids and ensures token migration backwards compatibility. Follow-up task assigned to INT-44102.
next_steps: 1) Eng to implement rotation-safe dedupe logic (assigned INT-44102) - target ETA 2026-03-18
2) Auth team to run a one-time backfill to reissue drilldown tokens for affected digest run_ids and add migration tooling - target ETA 2026-03-15
3) Run internal postmortem with BrightRoute engineering and update the Alert Fingerprint Rotation runbook to include compaction/backfill guardrails
